[FACT] User is a new senior software engineer.  
[PREFERENCE] User is looking for tips on effective leadership and team management.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended books for effective leadership and team management:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Phoenix Project" by Gene Kim, Kevin Behr, and George Spafford.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us" by Daniel H. Pink.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Five Dysfunctions of a Team" by Patrick Lencioni.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Radical Candor: Be a Kick-Ass Boss Without Losing Your Humanity" by Kim Scott.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "The Manager's Path: A Guide for Tech Leaders Navigating Growth and Change" by Camille Fournier.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Peopleware: Productive Projects and Teams" by Tom DeMarco and Timothy Lister.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Software Engineering at Google: Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time" by Titus Winters, Tom Manshreck, and Hyrum Wright.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended online resources for leadership and team management:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Pragmatic Engineer (blog by Gergely Orosz).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Software Engineering Daily (daily newsletter).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Leading by Design (blog by Lara Hogan).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Engineering Management (subreddit).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Coursera's Software Engineering Specialization (online courses).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips for effective leadership:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Seek mentorship.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Practice active listening.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Lead by example.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Communicate effectively.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Empower your team.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Foster a culture of feedback.  
[USER] Asked about common mistakes new senior software engineers make when leading a team.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Common mistakes include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Micromanaging.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Lack of clear communication.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Not empowering team members.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Focusing too much on technical details.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Not prioritizing team member growth and development.
